plan: Second-price rule: pay highest competing bid if we win. Dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit and avoid negative surplus. With value $3, bidding higher risks winning and paying above 3 if rivals bid between 3 and my bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable wins when rivals bid below 3. Discrete 0.1 increments don’t change the dominance of truthful bidding. With only 1 round, no learning or reputation effects matter. Therefore, bid exactly my value: 3.0.

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction (pay the highest competing bid). With independent private values, bidding your true value is a (weakly) dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. Ties are random; nudging above value to break ties is not worth the risk of negative surplus. With no history and one round, bid truthfully at $24. ]

Second-price (Vickrey) auction: winner pays the highest competing bid. In such auctions, bidding my true private value is a dominant strategy regardless of others’ behavior. My value is 11, so bidding 11 maximizes expected profit and avoids overpaying or missing profitable wins. One-shot round; no history to adjust for. Ensure 0.1-increment compliance.
